paragraphs.text: Many employees now work from home for at least part of the week. For some, the freedom is welcome, but others find that the boundary between work and personal life quickly disappears.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: The most common piece of advice is to create a separate working area. Even a small table in a quiet corner helps the brain to connect that space with work, and makes it easier to stop at the end of the day.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: A regular routine is equally important. People who start and finish at the same times each day, and take proper breaks, report feeling less tired than those who work whenever they have a free moment.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Isolation is a problem that many home workers do not expect. Without casual conversations in the kitchen or corridor, people can feel cut off from their team. Short video calls that are not about work can help.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: Finally, home workers should check that their equipment is safe and comfortable. A chair that supports the back and a screen at eye level can prevent pain that often develops after months of working on a sofa.
paragraphs.label: E

headings.text: Having a dedicated place to work
Mixed feelings about a new way of working
